'''Jack Lewis, Baron Lewis of Newnham''', [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]],<ref name="frs">{{cite journal|last1=Clark|first1=Robin J. H.|last2=Raithby|first2=Paul R.|title=Jack Lewis, Baron Lewis of Newnham HonFRSC. 13 February 1928 — 17 July 2014|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|volume=62|year=2016|pages=299–322|issn=0080-4606|doi=10.1098/rsbm.2015.0022|doi-access=free}}</ref> [[Honorary Fellows of the Royal Society of Chemistry|HonFRSC]] (13 February 1928 – 17 July 2014) was an [[England|English]] [[chemist]] working mainly in the area of [[inorganic chemistry]].

==Education and personal life==
Educated at [[Furness Academy|Barrow Grammar School]], he graduated in 1949 with a bachelor's degree in chemistry from the [[University of London]], after which he moved to the [[University of Nottingham]] where he obtained his [[Ph.D.]]

In 1951 he married Elfreida "Freddie" Lamb (1928-2023). They had one son and one daughter. He also had four grandchildren.<ref name=whoswho/>

==Professional career==
In 1953 he was appointed lecturer at the [[University of Sheffield]] before returning to London in 1956 as a lecturer at [[Imperial College London]]. He was [[Professor]] of [[Chemistry]] at the [[University of Manchester]] from 1961 to 1967, [[University College London]] from 1967 to 1970, and the [[University of Cambridge]] from 1970 to 1995. He was also the first Warden of [[Robinson College, Cambridge|Robinson College]], the newest of the Cambridge colleges, from its foundation in 1977 until 2001.<ref name=whoswho>{{cite book| last=Black |first=A| title=Who's Who| url=https://archive.org/details/whoswhoannualbio1974lond | url-access=registration | publisher=A. & C. Black|location=London|year=1974|isbn=9780713613773}}</ref>

He was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1973|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 1973]]<ref name=frs/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://royalsociety.org/about-us/fellowship/fellows/ |title=Fellows |publisher=The Royal Society |access-date=10 October 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101007152855/http://royalsociety.org/about-us/fellowship/fellows/ |archive-date=7 October 2010 }}</ref>  and was awarded their [[Davy Medal]] in 1985,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.royalsoc.ac.uk/page.asp?id=1756|title=Davy archive winners 1989-1900|publisher=Royal Society|access-date=9 October 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071013044709/http://www.royalsoc.ac.uk/page.asp?id=1756|archive-date=13 October 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref> and their [[Royal Medal]] in 2004.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.royalsoc.ac.uk/page.asp?id=1750|title=Royal recent winners|publisher=Royal Society|access-date=9 October 2007|archive-date=17 December 2004|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041217183526/http://www.royalsoc.ac.uk/page.asp?id=1750|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was also an [[Honorary Fellows of the Royal Society of Chemistry|Honorary Fellow]] of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]],<ref name="RSCNews">{{cite journal|date=October 2014|title=Deaths|journal=RSC News|publisher=[[Royal Society of Chemistry]]|page=23}}</ref> and its president from 1986 to 1988.<ref name=ARU>{{cite web|url=http://www.anglia.ac.uk/ruskin/en/home/microsites/honorary/lewis_of_newnham.html|title=404 – Anglia Ruskin University|access-date=21 April 2015|archive-url=https://archive.today/20121222233427/http://www.anglia.ac.uk/ruskin/en/home/microsites/honorary/lewis_of_newnham.html|archive-date=22 December 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jack Lewis|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/jack-lewis|access-date=2022-02-10|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|language=en}}</ref> the [[National Academy of Sciences]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jack Lewis|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/jack-lewis-ujkxbm/|access-date=2022-02-10|website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref> and the [[American Philosophical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Member History|url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Jack+Lewis&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced|access-date=2022-02-10|website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref>

[[File:Os10C(CO)24 2-.png|thumb|right|260px|The anion [Os<sub>10</sub>C(CO)<sub>24</sub>]<sup>2−</sup>, prepared by the Jack Lewis laboratory.]]

He was knighted in 1982<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=48939 |date=2 April 1982 |page=4588}}</ref> and created '''Baron Lewis of Newnham''' of [[Newnham, Cambridgeshire|Newnham]] in the County of [[Cambridgeshire]] on 8 February 1989.<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=51643 |date=13 February 1989 |page=1851}}</ref> He was a member of the House of Lords, where he sat as a cross bencher and was a member of a number of Select Committees on Science and Technology. He was also a member of the Advisory Council for the [[Campaign for Science and Engineering]].<ref name="CaSE Advisory Council">{{cite web|url=http://www.sciencecampaign.org.uk/about/who/advisory.htm |title=Advisory Council of the Campaign for Science and Engineering |access-date=2011-02-11 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100828110110/http://www.sciencecampaign.org.uk/about/who/advisory.htm |archive-date=28 August 2010 }}</ref> In 1993, he was made an Honorary Fellow of the [[University of Central Lancashire]].<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.uclan.ac.uk/corporate_information/honorary_fellows.php |title=Honorary Fellows | publisher = [[University of Central Lancashire]] |work=uclan.ac.uk |access-date=15 January 2015}}</ref> In 1995, he was awarded an Honorary Degree (Doctor of Science) by the [[University of Bath]].<ref>{{cite web  |url=http://www.bath.ac.uk/ceremonies/hongrads/  |title=Honorary Graduates 1989 to present  |publisher=[[University of Bath]]  |work=bath.ac.uk  |access-date=18 February 2012  |archive-date=17 July 2010  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100717061336/http://www.bath.ac.uk/ceremonies/hongrads/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 1998 he became the fourth Chairman of the Standing Committee on Structural Safety, serving until 2002.

==Scholarship==
Lewis's early career was dedicated to magnetic properties of metal complexes.  He achieved significant acclaim for contributions to [[metal carbonyl cluster]]s. Together with his longtime collaborator [[Brian F. G. Johnson]], his research group discovered many structurally unusual compounds.  Illustrative of their achievements is their synthesis of super tetrahedron [Os<sub>10</sub>C(CO)<sub>24</sub>]<sup>2−</sup>.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Jackson|first1=Peter F.|last2=Johnson|first2=Brian F. G.|last3=Lewis|first3=Jack|last4=Nelson|first4=William J. H.|last5=McPartlin|first5=Mary|title=The synthesis of the cluster dianion [Os10C(CO)24]<sup>2−</sup> by pyrolysis. X-Ray structure analysis of [N(PPh<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>]<sub>2</sub>[Os<sub>10</sub>C(CO)<sub>24</sub>] and [Os<sub>5</sub>C(CO)<sub>14</sub>H(NC<sub>5</sub>H<sub>4</sub>)]|journal=Journal of the Chemical Society, Dalton Transactions|date=1982|issue=10|pages=2099|doi=10.1039/DT9820002099}}</ref>

== Legacy ==

When Lewis died, Robinson College flew its flag at [[half mast]].<ref name="Gamlen">{{cite journal|last=Gamlen|first=G|date=April 2015|title=A Great Man|journal=RSC News|publisher=[[Royal Society of Chemistry]]}}</ref> A memorial service in his memory was held in the college's chapel on 28 February 2015,<ref name="Gamlen" /> the day after a symposium on his work, chaired by Emeritus Professor [[Brian F. G. Johnson|Brian Johnson]].<ref name="LLMS">{{cite web|url=https://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/news/lord-lewis-memorial-symposium|title=Lord Lewis Memorial Symposium|publisher=[[University of Cambridge]]|access-date=21 April 2015}}</ref> A staircase erected in his honour in the chapel is inscribed with his name and the words "his wisdom shaped this college".<ref name="Gamlen" /> Donations in his memory were used to create the "Lewis Research Studentship in Chemistry", a three-year graduate studentship in Chemistry at Robinson College.<ref name="LLMS" />
